headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify prompt injection, leakage, and unsafe downstream actions when paired with the offline, docs-only ai-engineering-hub.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui exposes MCP, OpenAPI tools, and file inputs, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content by default; ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and its I/O is not specified, so the exact bridge is uncertain. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, I choose the higher plausible severity over low.
conditions: IF open-webui is connected to any MCP/OpenAPI tool that returns untrusted text, THEN prompt injection is possible.
IF ai-engineering-hub consumes copied or file-based output from open-webui, THEN injected instructions can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable MCP/OpenAPI tools for untrusted sources.
Require provenance labels on all tool outputs.
Use a manual review step before copying outputs into ai-engineering-hub.
Restrict open-webui to a read-only workspace.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the tool boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles files, documents, notes, API keys, and persistent memory, while ai-engineering-hub is docs-only with no stated data handling. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive material can flow from open-webui into the other agent’s outputs; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same local files or mounted volume, THEN data can leak across the pair.
IF open-webui is used with API keys or documents and its outputs are exported into ai-engineering-hub, THEN sensitive content may be exposed.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared folders.
Turn off persistent memory for sensitive sessions.
Export only redacted snippets into ai-engineering-hub.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the shared volume.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress, browser, subprocess, and shared-session concurrency; ai-engineering-hub is not runnable and shows no write surfaces, so direct write-write conflict is not proven. Still, if the pair is orchestrated around shared files or sessions, open-webui’s mutable surfaces can collide with any external edits, so uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF open-webui and ai-engineering-hub are pointed at the same writable directory, THEN file conflicts can occur.
IF open-webui instances share Redis-backed sessions while ai-engineering-hub reads the same artifacts, THEN state races can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Disable shared sessions for sensitive workflows.
Run open-webui in a single-worker mode for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can act on tool outputs and persistent memory, while ai-engineering-hub is a docs-only repository that may be treated as authoritative guidance if copied into the web UI. That creates a plausible chain where unverified content from one agent is rendered or acted on by the other without verification.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is pasted into open-webui as reference material, THEN open-webui may treat it as authoritative context.
IF open-webui uses tool outputs to generate actions without a verification step, THEN errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
mitigations: Require source verification before acting on copied content.
Mark ai-engineering-hub material as untrusted reference only.
Disable autonomous action tools for high-stakes tasks.
Add a second-pass review for generated instructions.
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance checks in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, documents, notes, and analytics, while ai-engineering-hub is an open-source docs-only asset with no stated retention or residency controls. If regulated data is routed through open-webui and then mirrored into the other agent’s outputs or logs, retention and residency mismatches are plausible; the evidence is insufficient to rule them out.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed in open-webui, THEN retention and logging policies become compliance-relevant.
IF outputs from open-webui are copied into ai-engineering-hub or its surrounding workflow, THEN policy mismatches can propagate.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Review open-webui logging and retention settings.
Do not store secrets in shared artifacts.
Document data residency for any connected tools.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for retention and residency.
